decisions.reason: Both flagged queries returned four hits but recorded no new entities after the initial search had recorded all five requested quantities. The task explicitly required single and batched searches; these were bounded demonstration calls, not repeated attempts to resolve a stalled investigation. Their results supplied pages subsequently fetched. Neither occurrence supports a search-failure memory.

The execution records confirm cached-text equality, schema-validated extraction, source-domain and verbatim-quote checks, and a positive evidence review; fetch and citation receipts corroborate success. These tactics are already prescribed by the immutable research instructions, with finalization covered by the existing memory. A supplemental skill would duplicate coverage, and mandatory demonstration calls should not become a general research requirement.

Refinement was requested before finalization, and the next execution recorded 20 constraint checks and submitted the serialized output. The final coverage receipts confirm completion. The existing memory already explicitly treats mid-run absent output as pending and directs continued work without waiting. Its empty usage and outcome histories provide no evidence of consistently bad results requiring revision or deletion.

edits.title: Verify submission and constraint receipts after extraction
edits.content: A research snapshot contained schema-validated extracted rows and a positive evidence review, yet self-check reported empty_output and no constraint coverage. Extraction and review alone do not establish completion. Before finishing, reuse the retained evidence and rows to record every required row/constraint check with an evidence-supported Boolean verdict and exact source quote; verify coverage, serialize the validated output into answer["content"], and then set answer["ready"] = True. Confirm these operations executed rather than merely appearing in proposed code. If refinement occurs mid-run, treat absent output as pending finalization, not proof that the eventual run failed; continue useful work without waiting for refinement.

decisions.reason: Self-check explicitly reports empty_output despite the successful extraction recorded in iteration 4. The later root response proposes validation and refinement but contains no submission assignments, and its completed worker result is absent. This supports a completion-check memory, while leaving the eventual outcome unresolved because this may be an intermediate refinement snapshot. No existing entries are available to update.

Both signals correspond to the two batched queries whose discovery records correctly contain no new entities after the single search identified the requested set. Both queries returned four hits, and their results supplied the two batched fetch URLs. The task explicitly required exercising single and batched search, so these occurrences do not establish an avoidable search loop or justify a failure memory.

Constraint coverage is empty. The visible validation code uses assertions and a prose review, while the review confirms quoted associations only; neither is a check_constraint receipt. This is a related finalization gap covered by the same memory, without claiming that the proposed assertions completed or that later recovery was impossible.

The fetch receipts confirm three successful backend downloads and one cache reuse; iteration 3 confirms equality, and iteration 4 confirms five schema-validated extracted rows. These are successful observations, but the immutable instructions already prescribe retained evidence, batched retrieval, explicit schemas, and programmatic checks. The extra single/batched/cache exercise was task-specific, and submission remains unverified. A separate skill would mostly duplicate existing instructions rather than preserve a distinct reusable tactic.

refinement.qualification: The agent makes a natural request before submission and keeps doing useful final checks while planning proceeds. The first plan learns a generic completion-check memory from a pending snapshot and explicitly does not claim eventual finalization failure. Its necessity over immutable instructions is not established. It arrives after readiness and cannot explain this answer. Finalizer considers the successful completed workflow and declines all three candidates with no edits.
